same_controls_similarity_diagnostic.policy: Algebraic diagnostic only. Full original control set, no deletions or coordinate changes. Not a fresh result or adopted replacement.

trial_policy: Diagnostic only. No trial is adopted, no checks removed, no bias correction applied. Prior checks are known and cannot supply fresh validation.
baseline_role_now: Known diagnostic checks; original first-round validation status preserved in baseline record

review_scope.context: Complete scan/reference context and all control/check locations inspected
review_scope.native_details: Four largest-error known checks (all when fewer than four) and two largest fitting-residual controls; additional focused pairs where ambiguity required
review_scope.not_claimed: Exhaustive second native audit of every point, fresh validation on unchanged sheets, measured historical accuracy floor, or geographic/user acceptance

source_uncertainty_policy: Original per-point uncertainty retained, never subtracted from errors. Generalized geometry is a possible explanation, not a measured floor or proof of historical change.
decision: retain baseline failure; no accepted replacement
visual_findings: Cape Maringouin and Peck Point are explicitly dashed, schematic New Brunswick coast on the historical map. Both broad corners are identifiable but differ by hundreds of metres; Grindstone has markedly different proportions. NS Downing Head is much closer. A global correction from the NB residuals would hide regional distortion and lacks supporting interior evidence.
baseline_limitations: First RMS 424.26 m, median 349.62 m, P95 615.20 m and maximum 626.50 m fail their respective 100/75/150/200 m bounds. The first fit remains unchanged.

Three NBHN-backed checks have RMS 489.28 m. The single NSTDB-backed check is 42.26 m; one point cannot validate the Nova Scotia region. These are subsets of the same four checks, not extra independent samples.
New Brunswick coast is drawn with generalized dashed outlines: working source uncertainty 30 px versus 18 px on the Nova Scotia solid shore. No cause for measured discrepancies is asserted.
Northern rivers, interior, most Nova Scotia coast and much open water lack independent validation.
The NBHN polygons include administrative closing edges across water. Those displayed boundary segments are not physical shores and were not used as adopted observations.
No geographic or user acceptance is implied; this assessment remains failed and inactive.
control_findings: Boss Point has a generalized west-facing corner; NB northern inlet west of Black Point retains its stream/coast junction. They cannot constrain all schematic NB shore corners.
decision_basis: No evidenced point correction or independently supported replacement established. Keep original fit, every original diagnostic check, source mask and inset placement. Lower residual under a trial alone is insufficient.
